title: Charred Tomato Toast
deck: Hot tomatoes, crisp bread, olive oil and leaves that taste like summer.
steps: Dry the washed tomatoes. Heat a heavy frying pan over medium-high heat; toss tomatoes with half the olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Cook tomatoes in a single layer for 5–7 minutes, gently shaking the pan, until skins blister and split in places. Lower the heat if the oil begins to smoke.
Toast the bread until sturdy and golden on both sides. Gently rub each warm slice with the cut garlic.
Top the toast with the hot tomatoes and pan juices. Drizzle with remaining olive oil and finish with torn basil, salt and pepper. Serve at once.
note: Contains wheat/gluten in standard sourdough. Take care with hot oil.
equipment: Heavy frying pan, toaster or grill

title: Lemon & Herb Butter Beans
deck: Soft white beans lifted by lemon zest, good oil and handfuls of herbs.
steps: Rinse the drained beans and warm them gently with the water in a saucepan for 3–5 minutes. Avoid vigorous boiling.
Whisk the lemon juice, finely grated zest, olive oil, garlic and a pinch of salt.
Drain any excess bean water and gently fold the warm beans through the lemon dressing.
Add chopped parsley and black pepper. Taste, adjust the salt and loosen with a little warm water if needed. Serve warm in a shallow bowl.
note: Check canned-bean packaging for allergens and cross-contact.

title: Crispy Potato Salad
deck: Rough golden edges meet cool mustard yogurt and bright green dill.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C conventional / 200°C fan. Simmer the potatoes in salted water for roughly 12–15 minutes until just tender. Drain and let steam-dry for 5 minutes.
On an oiled metal tray, gently press each potato flat with the bottom of a sturdy glass. Keep the pieces connected.
Drizzle with olive oil and season. Roast for 30–35 minutes, turning the tray once, until crisp and golden at the edges.
Stir together yogurt, mustard, lemon juice and finely chopped dill. Season to taste.
Spread the dressing on a serving plate and pile the hot crisp potatoes on top just before eating.
note: Contains milk. Check mustard packaging for allergens. Oven trays become very hot.

title: Carrot, Orange & Fennel Salad
deck: A tangle of orange ribbons, crisp fennel and fresh citrus.
steps: Peel the carrots into long thin ribbons, and finely shave the trimmed fennel using a peeler or guarded mandoline.
Remove orange peel and white pith. Cut segments free over a bowl, keeping any released juice.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice and about 15 ml of orange juice with salt and pepper.
Gently toss carrots, fennel and orange segments with dressing. Arrange loosely on a broad plate and finish with parsley.
note: Use a guard with a mandoline or sharp peeler.

title: Roasted Pepper & Tomato Pasta
deck: Sweet roasted peppers and tomatoes clinging to every ribbon.
steps: Heat oven to 210°C conventional / 190°C fan. Cut and deseed peppers, halve the tomatoes and place with unpeeled garlic on a tray. Toss with 25 ml olive oil and a little salt.
Roast for 25–30 minutes until the edges blister and tomatoes soften. Cool briefly and squeeze garlic from its skins.
Blend the roasted vegetables to a thick sauce or crush roughly. Simmer in a large pan with the remaining oil for 3–5 minutes.
Cook ribbon pasta in well-salted boiling water according to the packet until al dente. Reserve a little water before draining.
Toss the pasta with sauce, adding reserved water a little at a time until glossy. Finish with torn basil and pepper.
note: Contains wheat/gluten in standard pasta. Take care when blending hot ingredients.
equipment: Oven, roasting tray, blender, pot, wide pan

title: Harissa Chickpea Skillet
deck: A warm skillet of chickpeas, greens and gentle fire.
steps: Heat oil in a deep skillet and soften the diced onion for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and harissa; stir for 30–60 seconds until fragrant without burning.
Add chopped tomatoes, drained chickpeas and water. Simmer gently for 10–12 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Fold in spinach in batches until wilted, about 2 minutes. Taste before adding more salt; harissa varies in salt and heat.
Serve from the skillet placed on a heat-safe trivet.
note: Harissa heat and allergens vary by product. The skillet handle may be hot.

title: Crispy Aubergine & Herbed Yogurt
deck: Deeply browned aubergine, cool yogurt and a little crunch.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C conventional / 180°C fan. Halve aubergines lengthwise, score the flesh shallowly and season.
Heat around 30 ml of olive oil in an ovenproof pan. Sear the aubergine halves cut-side down for 5–7 minutes until deeply browned.
Move the pan to the oven, or transfer the aubergines to a tray, and roast for 20–25 minutes until fully tender.
Mix thick yogurt with lemon, grated garlic, chopped parsley, remaining olive oil, salt and pepper.
Spread the herbed yogurt over a plate, top with roasted aubergine and scatter toasted sesame over it.
note: Contains milk and sesame. Use an ovenproof pan; the handle stays hot.
equipment: Ovenproof skillet or baking tray, mixing bowl

title: Golden Roast Chicken & Lemon
deck: Crisp, golden and meant for the middle of the table.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C conventional / 180°C fan. Keep the fully thawed chicken refrigerated until needed. Do not wash raw chicken.
Pat it dry with paper towel. Coat with oil, salt and pepper and place breast-up in a roasting tray. Arrange lemon quarters, halved garlic head and thyme around the bird without stuffing the cavity.
Roast roughly 75–100 minutes, shielding overly dark skin with foil. The time is only a guide; check actual internal temperatures with a food thermometer.
Confirm at least 74°C / 165°F in the thickest breast and the innermost thigh and wing without touching bone. Continue roasting and recheck any lower area.
Rest on a clean tray for about 15 minutes before carving. Keep cooked food separate from the raw preparation tools.
note: Food safety: raw poultry cross-contamination risk. Cook until a thermometer reads at least 74°C / 165°F in the thickest breast and innermost thigh and wing; time and skin colour alone are not proof. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.

title: Tomato & Saffron Rice
deck: Golden grains under soft red tomatoes and green herbs.
steps: Soak saffron in 60 ml of the measured hot stock for 5 minutes. Heat the oven to 200°C conventional / 180°C fan if oven-roasting the tomatoes.
Toss tomatoes with 15 ml of olive oil and roast around 20 minutes until softened, or blister in a skillet.
Soften chopped onion in 20 ml olive oil, add garlic, then stir in the rinsed and drained rice for 1 minute.
Add the measured stock, including the saffron infusion. Cover and cook over low heat about 12–15 minutes or as directed by rice packaging, until absorbed.
Rest covered off the heat 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and top with tomatoes and fresh parsley.
note: Some vegetable stocks contain allergens. Cool leftover cooked rice promptly; do not leave at room temperature.
equipment: Lidded saucepan, oven tray or skillet

title: Orange Olive Oil Cake
deck: A soft golden crumb and all the brightness of orange.
steps: Heat oven to 175°C conventional / 155°C fan. Grease and line one 20 cm round cake pan.
Whisk together flour, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl.
Whisk eggs and sugar in another bowl until slightly thickened, then gradually whisk in olive oil, yogurt, measured orange juice, fine zest and vanilla.
Fold the dry mixture gently into the wet ingredients just until no flour remains. Pour into the prepared pan.
Bake about 35–45 minutes until the centre springs back and a skewer shows no wet batter. Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then further on a rack before slicing.
note: Contains wheat, eggs and milk. This formula has not been kitchen-tested; verify before public culinary publication.
equipment: 20 cm round cake pan, parchment, bowls, whisk

title: Honey-Roasted Pears
deck: Amber edges, cool yogurt and a little honey.
steps: Heat oven to 190°C conventional / 170°C fan. Halve the pears and remove their cores.
Mix melted butter, honey, lemon juice and cinnamon. Place pear halves cut-side up in a snug dish with the water.
Spoon honey glaze over pears and roast for 25–35 minutes, basting once or twice, until tender and browned at the edges.
Serve one warm pear half per person with thick cool yogurt, roasting syrup and roughly chopped toasted walnuts.
note: Contains milk and walnuts. Hot sugar syrup can burn; honey is not suitable for infants under 12 months.

title: Dark Chocolate Tahini Cookies
deck: Deep cocoa, roasted sesame and a tender middle.
steps: Mix flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt. In a separate bowl beat softened butter, tahini and brown sugar until well combined.
Beat in the egg and vanilla. Fold in the dry mixture until it forms a dough; chill about 20 minutes if too soft to shape.
Heat oven to 175°C conventional / 155°C fan. Line a tray with parchment and divide dough into 12 evenly spaced mounds. Flatten lightly and add sesame seeds.
Bake about 10–12 minutes until edges are set but centres remain slightly soft. Cool on tray for 10 minutes before moving to a rack.
note: Contains wheat, milk, egg and sesame. Do not eat raw flour or raw cookie dough.
equipment: Baking tray, parchment, mixing bowls, whisk
